canonical.title: Which React table component to use in 2026

siblings.title: The 2026 React table landscape: headless vs batteries-included vs commercial grid
siblings.summary: Only four candidates are genuinely alive in 2026 — TanStack Table, AG Grid, MUI X Data Grid and react-data-grid — and the real axis is not features but how many weeks of table you agree to write yourself.

siblings.title: React tables at row scale: where the ceilings actually are
siblings.summary: Row count is almost never the constraint that breaks a React grid — update frequency, referential stability and the browser's 33.5M-pixel scroll cap are.

siblings.title: Server-driven data: which React table actually does the work for you
siblings.summary: AG Grid's Server-Side Row Model and MUI X's Data Source are real server-driven engines; TanStack Table only gives you manual* opt-outs and hands you the state machine.

siblings.title: Enterprise React data-grid features and what they actually cost in 2026
siblings.summary: AG Grid Enterprise at $999/dev perpetual is the cheapest way to buy row grouping + pivot + Excel export; building the same on TanStack Table costs 25-50 dev-days, so buy wins below ~40 developers.

siblings.title: Styling and design-system fit: which React grid bends to your design system?
siblings.summary: If the design system is authoritative, go headless (TanStack Table, or shadcn's copy-paste wiring of it); grid-owned CSS is only worth it when you're buying AG Grid's feature set, and MUI X / Mantine grids are design-system adoptions, not component adoptions.

sources.title: Handsontable — software licence
sources.claim: Handsontable is not open source; its free tier is a non-commercial licence barring production use connected to commercial activity.

sources.title: TanStack — AG Grid partnership
sources.claim: TanStack's own docs point you at AG Grid when you need grouping, pivoting or a server-side row model.

sources.title: AG Grid — licensing
sources.claim: Grouping, pivoting, aggregation, Excel export and the Server-Side Row Model are gated behind AG Grid Enterprise.

sources.title: MUI X — server-side aggregation
sources.claim: MUI gates server-side aggregation behind Premium.

sources.title: AG Grid — row models
sources.claim: Every virtualized grid renders roughly 40 rows regardless of dataset size.

sources.title: MUI X — virtualization
sources.claim: Browsers cap scroll-container height at 33.5M px (17.5M in Firefox), hard-limiting any natively-scrolling grid to roughly 500k–900k rows.

sources.title: GitHub — TanStack Virtual issue 616
sources.claim: TanStack Virtual has the same open scroll-height ceiling issue.

sources.title: GitHub — mui-x issue 10952
sources.claim: MUI X users report the grid degrading to unusable at ~10 updates/second on a 400-row window.

sources.title: AG Grid — high-frequency updates
sources.claim: AG Grid batches streaming updates outside React entirely.

sources.title: RevoGrid — Battle of the rows
sources.claim: Vendor-authored benchmark; contradicts LyteNyte's on whether AG Grid handles 100k rows comfortably.

sources.title: 1771 Technologies — performance benchmarks
sources.claim: LyteNyte's vendor-authored benchmark; contradicts RevoGrid's.

sources.title: AG Grid — theming with CSS
sources.claim: AG Grid plumbs design tokens through `--ag-*` custom properties, and warns class-level overrides are fragile because its DOM changes each release.

sources.title: GitHub — Tailwind CSS discussion 20306

sources.title: GitHub — TanStack Table issue 4797
sources.claim: With `manualPagination` plus `manualFiltering`, `pageIndex` is not reset when filters change — a user on page 1000 silently gets an empty result set.
